items.snippet: To evaluate the effect of access to AI on student exam performance, we recruited students who were taking either of these classes in the spring of 2023.
Sixteen out of fifty-two students taking Insurance Law (roughly 31%) completed the study, while thirty-two out of 128 students taking Introduction to American Law (roughly 23%) completed the study.
For Introduction to American Law and Legal Reasoning, thirty-nine students indicated they would be part of the study, and thirty-two students ultimately completed the study.
For each exam that was graded for this study, the grader filled in a detailed grading rubric that assigned specific points for different elements of the exam answer.
In Insurance Law, eighteen students responded to recruiting e-mails, and sixteen in fact completed the study.
For our main analyses, we used a set of 2,133 medical cases and 40,762 differential diagnoses from qualified physicians with different levels of professional experience (Materials and Methods).

The medical experts consisted of 1,370 attending physicians (37.3%), 139 fellows (3.8%), and 2,160 resident physicians (58.9%), representing senior doctors, doctors undergoing specialized training, and doctors in training, respectively.

Therefore, we report several accuracy metrics, including top-5, top-3, and top-1 accuracy, where a differential diagnosis is evaluated as correct if the correct diagnosis is among the top five, top three, or top one diagnoses, respectively (and the accuracy is the proportion of such cases).
